episode.tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
episode.title: What Is Artificial Intelligence?
episode.disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario. Wouri Express and its people are invented; the setting draws on documented conditions in Douala, Cameroon.

onScreen.text: Thirty drivers. One hundred and fifty messages a week.
onScreen.emphasis: Nobody knows why Thursdays run late.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Mbella runs Wouri Express, a small delivery company in Douala. Thirty drivers send her one hundred and fifty messages a week.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Every Thursday, deliveries run late. Nobody can say why. The answer is in those messages, and nobody has time to read them.

onScreen.title: What Is Artificial Intelligence?
onScreen.subtitle: AI Fundamentals · Lesson 1 · Built with a delivery company in Douala

messages.text: Ekambi: Port gate queue again. Two hours. Pharmacy delivery will be late.
Moukoko: Road at Bonabéri flooded after the rain. Turning back.

ui.title: Mbella's ask
lines: A weekly summary of the delivery reports
The delays that keep coming back
No new app for the drivers

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Tanyi, the drivers already write everything: port queues, flooded roads, customers not there. It is all in the group chat.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Mbella wants two things: a weekly summary, and the delays that keep coming back. And no new app for her drivers.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Ordinary software follows rules a person wrote. Late means more than two hours. It cannot read port gate queue again.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Artificial intelligence is software that learned patterns from many examples. So it can read messy human text and sort it by cause.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: It finds patterns. It does not decide who is at fault. That stays with Mbella.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Ordinary software takes rules from a person and does exactly that. Nothing more.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: An AI model is built differently. It was shown thousands of examples, and it learned the patterns inside them.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: So when a new message arrives, it can recognise: this is a port delay, this is a flood, this is a customer problem.

onScreen.title: Kito sorts one week of messages

steps.title: Read the messages
steps.detail: One week, one hundred and fifty lines

items.text: Port gate queue again. Two hours.
Road at Bonabéri flooded. Turning back.
Customer not at the shop. Waited forty minutes.

ui.title: Recurring
lines: Port gate: Tuesday and Thursday mornings

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: I read every message from the week. No new app, the drivers keep writing the way they do.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: And you put each one under a cause. Port, flood, customer. What if a message fits none of them?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Then it goes under not stated. I never invent a cause. Now the pattern shows: port gate queues, Tuesday and Thursday mornings.

messages.text: The truck broke down on the Bonabéri road.
Reason not stated. Driver message 88 only says: late, sorry.

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: Delivery eighty-eight? Obviously the truck broke down on the Bonabéri road. Case closed.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Nobody wrote that. Message eighty-eight only says late, sorry. So my answer is: reason not stated.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: AI finds patterns in what people recorded. If the drivers never wrote it, it cannot know it. So Mbella adds one tap: port, road, customer, other.

messages.text: What delayed us most this week?
Port gate queues, eleven deliveries, Tuesday and Thursday mornings. Source: driver messages 12, 15, 27, 40.

ui.title: Move Thursday port runs to the afternoon?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Mbella asks what delayed us most. I answer: port gate queues, eleven deliveries, Tuesday and Thursday mornings, with the message numbers.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Moving the port runs to the afternoon? That is a business decision. Mbella clicks, not the model.

items.label: Recruiting
items.text: Match applications to the job's needs

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Same idea elsewhere: a clinic sorting patient messages by urgency, a shop grouping complaints, a recruiter matching applications.

onScreen.title: Who owns this?
items: Wouri Express owns the messages and the results
Drivers are never named in a blame line
Mbella reviews every summary before acting
Accountable: the company, not the model

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Wouri Express owns its messages and its results. No driver is named in a blame line. Mbella reads every summary before she acts.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: That is artificial intelligence: software that learned patterns, reading what your people already write, with a person deciding.

onScreen.title: Your build challenge
items: Find one pile of messy text at work
Write the three causes you would sort it into
That list is the start of an AI system

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Your challenge: find one pile of messy text at your work, and write the three causes you would sort it into.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Don't just use AI. Build it to work reliably. Next: generative AI, explained simply.

tanyi.name: Tanyi
tanyi.role: AI engineer and instructor, the animated host. Middle-aged Black African man. Calm, direct, practical. Has built and operated real systems.

amara.name: Amara
amara.role: Curious learner who asks the questions beginners are thinking.

kito.name: Kito
kito.role: Small AI assistant who demonstrates concepts and occasionally makes believable mistakes.

hallucinator.name: The Hallucinator
hallucinator.role: Mischievous. Represents confident but incorrect AI output.

gatekeeper.name: The Gatekeeper
gatekeeper.role: Represents security, privacy, governance and human approval.
